title: Panel tagging and lightweight audit sketch
content:
Purpose
This is a pragmatic sketch for a lightweight panel tagging and minimal audit flow we can ship quickly. Goal: make panels self-describing, cheaply auditable, and cost-aware so oncall and dashboard owners can prune, triage, and annotate dashboards without a heavy governance process.

Background
We have many dashboards and semi-orphaned panels. Full signal curation playbooks exist, but teams need a lower-friction way to mark panels with provenance, cost footprint, owners, and TTL. This doc proposes a minimal schema, examples, an audit checklist, span/tracing naming guidance for inference paths, and an implementation rollout plan.

Minimal panel tag schema (fields to add to panel metadata)
- panel_owner: team or individual email (e.g., eng-observability / aisha@redwood.ai)
- intent: {alerting | investigation | smoke | business-metric} (single value)
- cost_bucket: {low | medium | high} (rough cost impact for queries per hour)
- data_ttl_days: integer (how long the underlying metrics are kept at full resolution)
- provenance: short text (ticket/feature/rollout id)
- last_reviewed: ISO date
- public_facing: {yes | no} (if product/CS uses it)
- sample_query: short SQL or query string to reproduce the panel

Why these fields
- owner + last_reviewed enable lazy auditing: if panel_owner doesn't respond and last_reviewed > 365 days, mark for archival.
- cost_bucket is intentionally coarse so teams can quickly label expensive panels (e.g., high-cardinality joins, long time ranges).
- sample_query + intent help oncall triage when investigating regressions.

Tracing and span hints for panel authors
When a panel visualizes a flow across the inference stack (API -> router -> model runtime -> kv cache -> fallback), prefer span names and tags that follow this pattern: 
- span.operation: inference.request | batch.dispatch | kv.fetch | model.exec
- span.model_variant: gpt-3.5-q4 | llama-2-13b-q8
- span.route_policy: latency-priority | cost-priority
- span.cache_hit: boolean
- span.request_size_tokens: integer
- span.kv_ttl_hint: seconds (if relevant)
These tags make it easy for dashboard panels to group traces by cache_hit or model_variant without brittle parsing.

Panel design heuristics to reduce cost
- Default panel time window to 1h or 6h for expensive queries, with a control to widen manually.
- Avoid raw-sample tables for high-cardinality labels; use sampled aggregates instead.
- Add a computed metric tokens_per_second instead of joining raw traces in the panel where possible.

Audit checklist (quick)
- [ ] owner present and reachable
- [ ] intent set
- [ ] cost_bucket set
- [ ] sample_query included and runnable
- [ ] last_reviewed <= 90 days for alerting panels
- [ ] linked rollout/ticket in provenance
- [ ] if public_facing=yes, security review link present

Example panel metadata (text to paste in panel description)
panel_owner: eng-formatting
intent: investigation
cost_bucket: medium
data_ttl_days: 30
provenance: OBS-482
last_reviewed: 2026-03-03
public_facing: no
sample_query: "SELECT bin, avg(latency_ms) FROM inference_latency WHERE model='gpt-3.5-q4' AND ts > now()-1h GROUP BY bin ORDER BY bin"

Automated audit job (sketch)
- Weekly job scans dashboards, extracts metadata fields
- Flags panels missing owner/intent or with last_reviewed older than threshold
- Emails owners with a templated form to self-certify or mark for archival
- After 30 days without response panels auto-archive to an internal archive folder (not deleted)

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Pilot with 3 teams (observability, serving-runtime, console) for 4 weeks. Provide a tiny UI helper to insert tags into panel descriptions.
2) Run audit job and do a one-time cleanup pass with the pilot teams.
3) Expand to 10 more teams; publish tagging cheat sheet and sample queries.
4) Bake tags into dashboard creation templates and alert runbooks.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should cost_bucket be computed heuristically (sample query cost estimation) or fully manual? Start manual, measure consistency, then explore heuristics.
- What is the archival retention policy for panels removed from main dashboards? Proposed: keep archived dashboards in read-only for 365 days.
- How to handle cross-team panels where ownership is shared? Allow comma-separated owners and a primary_owner field.

Next actions (as of authoring)
- Aisha: prototype a small script to extract panel descriptions and surface missing fields (due 2026-03-10)
- Marco: scope a minimal UI helper for inserting metadata into panel descriptions (due 2026-03-17)
- Priya: add a page in Confluence with the cheat sheet and examples (due 2026-03-12)

Notes to reviewers
This is intentionally lightweight: the aim is to lower friction so teams adopt tagging quickly. We can merge with larger signal curation playbooks later. Feedback welcome on the field names and whether we should expand the span tags recommended above.

Revision history
- 2026-02-18 initial sketch
- 2026-03-03 added audit checklist and rollout dates
